passages.context: CCC 1954-1960 (English): natural law expressing 'the original moral sense which enables man to discern by reason the good and the evil' (1954, quoting Leo XIII, Libertas praestantissimum); 'the divine and natural law' showing the way (1955, quoting Augustine and Aquinas); universality (1956, quoting Cicero, De re publica); varied application (1957); immutability (1958, quoting Augustine, Confessions); foundation for moral rules and civil law (1959); grace and revelation needed for natural law's precepts to be known 'by everyone with facility, with firm certainty and with no admixture of error' (1960, quoting Pius XII, Humani generis). Extracted verbatim from the exact fetched response.
